prompt:
PLAN 02 — THE FIRST LINE | THE VOICE ARRIVES

Create a 15-second cinematic sequence for Seedance 2.5.
Horizontal 16:9.
Exactly three shots lasting four, eight and three seconds.

CHARACTER REFERENCES:
Young Homayoun = {{CHAR_HOMAYOUN_YOUNG}}
Composer = {{CHAR_COMPOSER}}
Father = {{CHAR_FATHER}}

LOCATION REFERENCE:
Early-2000s recording studio, vocal booth and connected control room = {{LOC_RECORDING_STUDIO}}

PROP REFERENCES:
Mixing console = {{PROP_MIXING_CONSOLE}}
Studio microphone and pop filter = {{PROP_MIC}}
Studio headphones = {{PROP_HEADPHONES}}
Lyric sheet = {{PROP_LYRIC_SHEET}}

AUDIO REFERENCE:
Original vocal performance of “می‌تراود مهتاب” = {{AUDIO_MITARAVAD_MAHTAB}}

Preserve the exact character appearance, studio geography, wardrobe, microphone placement, headphone design, lighting direction and blocking established in PLAN 01.

CONTINUITY START STATE:

Direct continuation from PLAN 01.

Homayoun remains inside the vocal booth at the microphone.

The headphones remain firmly over both ears.

He has just received the composer’s professional cue and his father’s quiet acknowledgement.

The composer remains seated behind the mixing console inside the control room.

The father remains standing separately in the control room.

Homayoun now turns inward toward the act of singing.

SHOT 02A | 00:15–00:19 | PREPARATION

Cut to a 65mm intimate detail sequence from the front side of the microphone.

Begin on Homayoun’s hand gently stabilizing the lyric sheet.

Shift focus to the headphone cup enclosing his ear.

Continue toward his mouth positioned naturally behind the pop filter.

Finish on his eyes becoming still and focused.

These details communicate preparation and concentration rather than anxiety.

Homayoun takes one calm controlled breath.

His body becomes quiet.

SHOT 02B | 00:19–00:27 | “می‌تراود مهتاب”

Cut to a 40mm frontal medium shot directly facing Homayoun.

The microphone and pop filter remain centered naturally between camera and singer without covering his full face.

The headphones remain clearly visible on his head.

Begin a single slow, physically smooth forward camera move.

Travel gradually from medium framing toward an intimate close-up over the full eight seconds.

For the first three seconds, Homayoun lets the breath settle and prepares his mouth naturally.

Then he begins performing the supplied vocal recording of “می‌تراود مهتاب”.

Use the supplied audio as the exact performance source.

Match lip movement precisely to the original vocal timing, mouth shapes, syllable articulation, breath placement and phrasing.

The opening “می...” emerges softly and without theatrical emphasis.

As the phrase develops, his face opens almost imperceptibly.

The emotional transition is from concentrated readiness into quiet certainty.

He realizes through the act of singing that the room is truly listening to him.

Maintain the frontal camera path throughout the performance.

Keep Homayoun as the uninterrupted emotional center.

SHOT 02C | 00:27–00:30 | THE ROOM LISTENS

Cut briefly to a 65mm control-room composition through layered foreground equipment.

A VU meter responds clearly to Homayoun’s continuing voice in the foreground or near foreground.

Behind it, the composer remains seated at the console, partially obscured by equipment, shallow focus and glass reflection.

His face remains indistinct, but his still attentive posture makes it clear that he is listening closely.

The father occupies a separate deeper position elsewhere in the control room.

He watches quietly.

Neither man performs an exaggerated reaction.

The moment belongs to Homayoun’s voice.

End while the singing continues.

PERFORMANCE AND LIP-SYNC:

The supplied vocal recording is the absolute timing reference for Homayoun’s performance.

Preserve natural facial anatomy.

Lip articulation follows the exact Persian phonemes of the supplied performance.

Facial movement remains subtle and physically realistic.

The emotional change happens gradually through breath, focus, eyes and posture.

COMPOSER VISIBILITY:

The composer is never presented in a clean hero portrait.

Use console hardware, foreground objects, studio-glass reflections, three-quarter orientation, partial silhouette and controlled shallow focus to limit facial detail.

His professional presence must remain unmistakable even when precise facial likeness is understated.

LIGHT AND IMAGE:

Continue the same warm practical lighting from PLAN 01.

Soft highlights on microphone metal, headphone material, glass and console controls.

Natural exposure and restrained contrast.

The frontal singing shot becomes progressively more intimate as the camera approaches.

Keep the visual texture tactile, human and understated.

SOUND:

The supplied vocal recording enters during SHOT 02B and remains the dominant sound through the end.

Subtle studio room tone continues underneath.

Small breath detail before the first syllable.
Gentle electrical hum.
Natural console ambience.

ADDITIONAL MUSIC: none.
ADDITIONAL DIALOGUE: none.

<<<image_2>>> is Mohammad-Reza Shajarian (CHR-002 V01); match it wherever Mohammad-Reza Shajarian appears.
<<<image_3>>> is Musician (CHR-003 V01); match it wherever Musician appears.
<<<image_4>>> is Studio Control Room (LOC-001 V01); match it wherever Studio Control Room appears.
<<<image_5>>> is Studio Vocal Booth (LOC-002 V01); match it wherever Studio Vocal Booth appears.
<<<image_6>>> is Mixing Console (PRP-001 V01); match it wherever Mixing Console appears.
<<<image_7>>> is Audio Level Meter (PRP-002 V01); match it wherever Audio Level Meter appears.
<<<image_8>>> is Studio Headphones (PRP-004 V01); match it wherever Studio Headphones appears.
<<<image_9>>> is Sheet Music (PRP-006 V01); match it wherever Sheet Music appears.
